line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2
teaches: In a fianchetto system, answer a harmless flank pawn poke by simply continuing your development, not by reacting to it. Spending a move to prevent a pin would weaken a key square for no real gain — let the opponent's little pawn move be the wasted one.
explains: The bishop completes its fianchetto on g2, taking aim down the long diagonal. Meeting the rook-pawn nudge with a pawn move of your own would only soften the b4 square, so White just develops and waits for Black to commit.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O
teaches: The instinctive supporting pawn move is not always best. In this fianchetto setup, castling first is stronger than propping the centre with a modest pawn, because it keeps a tempo in hand for when the pin is traded off — and it leaves a tactical resource if the opponent gets greedy.
explains: Castling is the key move here, better than the natural d3. Once Black trades the bishop on c3, White recaptures toward the centre with a tempo and an open position, and there is even a tactic waiting if Black snatches the e4-pawn.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O Bxc3 dxc3
teaches: When you recapture, prefer the direction that opens a piece and grips the centre over the one that merely keeps the pawns tidy. A recapture toward the middle frees a bishop and stakes a bigger central claim.
explains: Taking back with the d-pawn opens the dark-squared bishop's diagonal and increases White's grip on the central squares, better than recapturing away from the centre. The doubled pawns are a small price for the activity.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 g3 a6 Bg2 Bb4 O-O Bxc3 dxc3 Nxe4 Nxe5
teaches: When the opponent grabs a pawn with a piece, look for the in-between capture that wins it straight back — and do not fear a desperado counter-grab. Counting the sequence out beats reflexively defending.
explains: If Black snatches the pawn on e4, the knight takes on e5 attacking the knight on c6, and White regains the material once the dust settles. A desperado counter-grab is nothing to be afraid of when you count the sequence out.
